answer: A lantern burns only at the flame it was lit from, and any lantern may give flame once ever: the haven signs the giving, the donor's light halves for good, and the meadow meters every burn so no head hides its true light. A clone cut from copied flame stands dim; to run one at full work, its operator must buy out a distinct bright donor — repaying the discounted light the split snuffs — and the k-th clone bids into a donor pool one rank thinner each time.
